subject: MedFlux: audit/retention/BYOK questions — triage and exception path
thread_summary: MedFlux asks for audit log schema, retention guarantees, BYOK/KMS options, and a documented exception path for a short-term retention carveout during POC. Internal triage covers product capabilities, a temporary escrow option, rollout implications, and a clear owner for supplier evidence delivery.
messages:
From: Laura Chen <security@medflux.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team has three immediate asks before we can move the POC to our test environment:

1) Audit log schema and retention options — we need to confirm what event types are emitted and whether we can get an export on demand (CSV or JSON).
2) Retention guarantees during the POC — our legal team wants clarity on short-term retention windows and the carveout process for ephemeral evidence.
3) BYOK/KMS — we’d like to know if we can provide keys or if escrow is required for audit evidence.

I attached our security questionnaire (medflux_ssq.pdf). Can you triage and tell us what is product capability vs. an exception/implementation ask? Also include the likely timeline and a recommended fallback while we evaluate options.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Sr. InfoSec Manager | MedFlux Health
security@medflux.com

Attachments: medflux_ssq.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2028-10-09T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC

Team, forwarding MedFlux’s SSQ. High level: they want audit schema + export, temporary retention clarity, and a BYOK path or escrow. Can we do a quick triage here?

Specific asks:
- Which events are included in our audit export today (admin actions, model calls, embeddings access, token-level metadata)?
- Can we provide on-demand exports for a tenant? Format preference is CSV/JSON.
- For a short POC (30-90 days), do we support a retention carveout or ephemeral escrow? If not, what is the recommended temporary workaround that meets their compliance bar?
- BYOK: what are the supported key management patterns (Customer-managed KMS, HSM/KMS integrations, transient escrow)?

Please reply with: capability / workaround / implementation ETA / owner. I’ll consolidate and reply to Laura.

- Mateo
Director, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC

Thanks Mateo. Quick notes from product side:

- Audit export: product currently emits admin events, model invocation metadata (model name, prompt id, timestamps), errors, and auth events. We do NOT surface token-level content in exports for hosted customers. We can produce per-tenant JSON/CSV exports on-demand via the Console (manual export) or programmatically via the exports API — ETA for a documented API endpoint is Q4 if customer wants an integration.

- Retention: default retention is 90 days for hosted trial accounts; we support configurable retention for Dedicated/Private. For POC we can do an administrative short-term extension (120 days) as an exception if legal signs an MSA addendum. Need CS to own the exec approval.

- BYOK/KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported on Private and Dedicated. Hosted API has a sealed-key model; we can offer escrow of audit exports into a customer-controlled S3 bucket (encrypted by customer KMS) as an interim. That escrow flow is an ops playbook today, not fully self-serve.

Action items: 
1) Marissa to confirm exact audit event list and produce sample-audit-export.csv.
2) Jonas to draft proposed exception language for a 120-day POC retention addendum and estimate legal review time.
3) Naomi to confirm the ops runbook for escrow exports and steps for customer KMS encryption.

ETA: I can have the sample export and ops steps by EOD tomorrow. Jonas, can you pick up the addendum draft?

- Grace
Sr PM, Product Compliance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-10T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC

Done. Draft attached in-thread (summary below).

Summary of proposed POC addendum (for legal):
- Limited exception: extend hosted retention to 120 days for account MDFX-POC-2028 for the duration of the evaluation.
- Evidence escrow: Redwood will export audit logs weekly to a customer-controlled S3 bucket provided by MedFlux; customer must apply KMS encryption keys on their bucket.
- Data scope: exports limited to admin events, model metadata, auth events, and error logs. No model input/output content will be included in the audit export for hosted mode.
- Timebox and revocation: exception expires after 90 days unless extended by mutual written agreement.
- Liability and access: standard Redwood data processing terms apply; any deviation requires Legal approval.

ETA: I can circulate a one-page addendum to Laura by COB Tuesday if no major blockers.

- Jonas
Lead, Security & Compliance Operations

Attachments: draft-addendum-for-MDFX.txt

From: Laura Chen <security@medflux.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medflux.com
Date: 2028-10-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC

Thanks all for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points before we sign any addendum:

- The export scope is acceptable if the "no model I/O" restriction is explicit in the addendum.
- We prefer weekly exports but need the option to request an ad-hoc export within 48 hours. Can you add that to the ops runbook?
- For escrow: MedFlux will provide the S3 bucket and KMS keys. We need a small proof-of-concept run to validate encryption and retrieval.
- Please include estimated lead times per item (sample export, ops runbook, legal addendum) in your reply so procurement can align approvals.

If you can send a consolidated reply with owners and dates, we’ll prepare the internal approvals.

Best,
Laura

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <security@medflux.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, procurement@medflux.com
Date: 2028-10-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit logs, retention & BYOK options for MedFlux POC — consolidated next steps

Laura — consolidating next steps and owners below: 

1) Sample audit export (plan + sample CSV) — Owner: Marissa Cole. ETA: 2028-10-10 EOD (sample delivered) — DONE. File: sample-audit-export.csv.
2) Ops runbook for escrow + ad-hoc export (48 hour ad-hoc process) — Owner: Naomi Feldman. ETA: 2028-10-12 COB.
3) Draft POC retention addendum (explicit "no model I/O" clause + weekly export cadence + revocation terms) — Owner: Jonas Weber. ETA: 2028-10-12 COB (one-page).
4) Technical POC for S3/KMS pipeline (validate encryption + retrieval) — Owner: Mateo Alvarez (coordination)/MedFlux infra. ETA: Schedule within 3 business days after S3 details are provided.

We’ll attach the sample export and the draft addendum in the next message. Please confirm if the timelines above work for procurement/legal at MedFlux. If they need accelerated timelines, let us know and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks — Mateo

Attachments: sample-audit-export.csv (CSV, 18KB), draft-addendum-for-MDFX.txt (TXT, 3KB)
